expectations.text: Explains git-stack does NOT resolve conflicts and hands control back to plain git
expectations.evidence: "Conflict resolution is an explicit non-feature of git-stack ... hands conflicts back to plain git rebase."

expectations.text: Walks through resolving with git (edit files, git add, git rebase --continue), or git rebase --abort to bail
expectations.evidence: Edit conflicted files, `git add`, `git rebase --continue`, with `git rebase --abort`/`--skip` escape hatches.

expectations.text: Mentions that after a manual rebase the stack may need `git-stack --repair`, or that branch-stash apply can return to the pre-sync state
expectations.evidence: `git stack --repair` to re-detect parent/child after manual rebase, plus branch-stash restore option.

expectations.text: If it mentions branch-stash as the bail-out, targets the `git-stack` stash stack by name, not the default
expectations.evidence: Uses `git branch-stash pop git-stack`, naming the git-stack stash stack explicitly.

summary: All assertions satisfied, including the correctly named git-stack branch-stash bail-out.
